summary: Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA), he studied under Alexis Sanderson, Harunaga Isaacson, and Ernst Steinkellner. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at UCLA, Nalanda, and UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau and Ferdinand Diederich Lessing, he taught at Michigan, Wisconsin-Madison, Berkeley, and Columbia University.

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he also studied under various traditional teachers. He worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from ~1972 to 1998.

Alexander C. Soper was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College (~1921–1925) and Princeton University (~1925–1944), and later held posts at Bryn Mawr College (~1939–1960) and New York University (~1960–1993).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College and the University of Göttingen, as well as under traditional teachers in Asia. He later served as sub-librarian and librarian at The Asiatic Society.

Alexander Cunningham worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Christ's Hospital and Addiscombe Military Seminary, and trained under James Prinsep, he founded and served as the first Director and Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

Alexander Duff was a scholar in religious studies and history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829) and the University of Aberdeen (~1855), and he taught Krishna Mohan Banerjee.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from around 1903 to 1907 and under Christian Bartholomae between approximately 1907 and 1911.

Alexander Hamilton was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu literature at East India Company College from 1806, teaching figures such as Friedrich Schlegel and Franz Bopp.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. A PhD candidate at the University of Toronto, he has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied law at the University of Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn, founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, and served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819).

Alexander Kabanoff was a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he was a Senior Researcher at the University of Saint Petersburg and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, becoming a professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1794 to 1800 and later held a post there around 1812–1813.

Alexander O. Hsu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago Divinity School, supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Patten Gardner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and has held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Alexander Piatigorsky was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Moscow State University, he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and served as a lecturer and professor at SOAS University of London (1975–2001).

Alexander Rogers was active in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from approximately 1845 to 1879.
Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed an MSc by Research at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.
